questions.question:
**Parts of the given sentence have been given as options. One of them contains a grammatical error. Select the option that has the error.**

When you have worked out this sum, you may went out to play.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part of the sentence is: **went out to play**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Replace **'went out'** with **'go out'** to make the sentence correct.
 
• The given sentence is written in the **Present Perfect tense**.
 
• **Structure of the Present Perfect Tense:** **Subject + have/has + past participle + the rest of the sentence.__**
 
• The **present perfect** in the **'if/when'** -clause of a sentence in the first conditional emphasises that **one action depends on the completion of another**.
 
 
• **Example -** *When I've finished writing my paper by tonight, I'll go out with my friends.*
 
 
 
• The phrase **'go out'** is often used this way to state that someone is going out to do something.
 
• **'Went out'** as a verb means Simple past tense.
 
• The given sentence states that **"After completing the sum, he may go out and play."**

​Therefore, the correct answer is **option 2**.

**Corrected sentence: ***When you have worked out this sum, you may** go out** to play.*

questions.question:
**Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence.**

Mahatma Gandhi is undoubtedly one of the __much__ popular authors of our times.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **most**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Replace '**much'** with '**most'** to make the sentence correct.
 
• **'Most'** denotes the greatest or highest degree, often used with an adjective or adverb to form the **superlative**. 
 
 
• **Example - ***Peter is one of the **most** reliable people on this planet.*
 
 
 
• **Superlative** adjectives are used to describe an object which is at the upper or lower limit of quality.
 
• The **comparative** form of '**much'** is** 'more'**, and the **superlative** form of '**much' **is the '**most'.**
 
• **'Much' **means a large amount, while **'most'** means the largest amount in comparison with other things.
 
 
• **Example - ***I will lend you as **much** money as you want.*
 
 
 
• **'One of the'** is always used with **superlatives** and it is used when we are referring to someone or something specific among many others.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 3**.

**Corrected sentence:** *Mahatma Gandhi is undoubtedly one of the **most** popular authors of our times. *

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Best** means the most excellent or desirable type or quality.
 
• **Total** means the whole number or amount of something.
 
• **Better **describes something as being superior or is an adverb that means something is done to a higher degree or more completely.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No substitution required’.**

Sheela __is trying__ for a job since last year.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **has been trying **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Replace** 'is trying'** with **'has been trying'** to make the sentence correct.
 
• **“Is trying”** refers to occurring in the present, at the present moment.
 
• **Structure of the Present Continuous Tense:** ***Subject + am/is/are + present participle (verb+ing) + the rest of the sentence__***
 __
 
• ​__**Example -** *The boys are playing in the park.*
 
 
 
• **“Has been trying”** refers to the **present perfect continuous**. It refers to a time period which began in the past and continues in the present and into the future.
 
• Structure of the Present Perfect Continuous Tense: *__**Subject + have/has + been + present participle + the rest of the sentence**__*
 
 
• **​Example -** *I have been watching TV since 7 pm.*
 
 
 
• We normally use **'since'** with the present perfect to describe an action or situation that **began in the past and continues in the present**.
 
• In the given sentence** 'since'** is used to mean that **"Sheela is continuously trying for a job for the last year and in present, the search is going on."**
 
• **'Has'** is used with the third person singular.

​Therefore, the correct answer is **option 4**.

**Corrected sentence:** *Sheela **has been trying** for a job since last year. *

questions.question:
**Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.**

A. However, after studying the myths scientifically, only a simpleton would find them irrational or worthless.

B. Moreover, it is wrong to analyse myths on the yardstick of their factual accuracy as they were designed to serve a greater, deeper purpose.

C. Myths have always been regarded as a complex and intriguing aspect in human life

D. In modern scientific world, they are essentially seen as something unscientific and meaningless.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"CDAB"**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Let's look at the correct sequence of the passage.
 
• **Statement C** is the opening sentence of the passage **which explains the theme of the passage that is Myths and it's importance.**
 
• **Statement D **is the second sentence of the passage **which explains that In today's world myths are describes as something unscientific and meaningless.**
 
• **Statement A** is the third sentence of the passage **which explains that myths also have great scientific values and only a foolish person would consider them irrational or worthless.**
 
• **Statement B** is the last sentence of the passage **which explains that people should not analyse myths on their factual accuracy and describes for what purposes myths are designed.**

Hence, the correct sequence is **C, D, A, B**

**The correct passage is:** **C.** *Myths have always been regarded as a complex and intriguing aspect in human life. **D.** In modern scientific world, they are essentially seen as something unscientific and meaningless.** A.** However, after studying the myths scientifically, only a simpleton would find them irrational or worthless. **B.** Moreover, it is wrong to analyse myths on the yardstick of their factual accuracy as they were designed to serve a greater, deeper purpose.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.**

I __had get back from __Hyderabad last month.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is:** got back from.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The rule is:** Present Perfect + Point of Time= Simple Past.**
 
• It should be noted that the **point of time** (last month) in the past demonstrates that the action took place at a point in the past.
 
• So, the **verb** that must be used should be in the **simple past tense**.
 
• The point of time in the past is mentioned by the following as given below:
 
 
• ago
 
• before
 
• yesterday
 
• the other day
 
• last month/year/day
 
 
 
• The use of 'had get back from' is grammatically incorrect as the point of time is present in the sentence.
 
• Thus, 'got back from' is the correct usage in this context.

Therefore, the corrected sentence is: I ***got back from*** __Hyderabad last month.

• **'Me'** is used by a speaker to refer to himself or herself as the object of a verb or preposition.
 
• **'Mine'** is used in place of another noun when it's understood what's being discussed and adds information describing whose it is.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **Confusion Points__**

 
• Both **my** and **mine** are possessives, but they are used rather differently.
 
• **'My'** is put before a noun to indicate the speaker's possession.
 
 
• **Example -** *You have your talent. I have **my** talent.*
 
 
 
• **Mine** is similar to **my**, but it cannot be used with the following noun the same way as **my**, it can't be put before a noun.
 
• **'Mine'** is always used after a helping verb to refer to something previously mentioned.
 
 
• **Example -** *You have your talent. I have **mine**.*
